prs.title: fix: allow integer file descriptors for errlog in stdio_client
prs.author: RudrenduPaul
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: sys.stderr cannot be passed to subprocess in Jupyter notebook environments because Jupyter replaces sys.stderr with a custom stream object that has no real OS-level file descriptor, causing subprocess creation to fail when errlog defaults to sys.stderr. (2 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: sys.stderr cannot be passed to subprocess in Jupyter notebook environments because Jupyter replaces sys.stderr with a custom stream object that has no real OS-level file descriptor, causing subprocess creation to fail when errlog defaults to sys.stderr. (2 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: PR #2410 solves the root issue by widening the errlog parameter type from TextIO to TextIO | int, letting callers pass subprocess.DEVNULL (an integer) to discard stderr or any other integer FD — a general fix that works for Jupyter, CI environments, and any other context where sys.stderr lacks a file descriptor. PR #2020 instead adds a _is_jupyter_environment() heuristic that inspects IPython internals (IPKernelApp config key, ZMQInteractiveShell class name) to detect the environment at runtime; this approach is fragile across IPython versions and doesn't cover non-Jupyter environments with the same underlying constraint. #2410's diff is also smaller (type annotation + docstring change), has no new runtime dependencies, and gives library users explicit control rather than relying on detection logic.

prs.title: fix(stdio): handle BrokenResourceError in stdout_reader race (#1960)
prs.author: ddullah
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: BrokenResourceError (and ConnectionResetError) raised inside stdout_reader when the stdio_client context exits while the subprocess is still writing — the stream is already closed when send() is called, causing an unhandled exception that surfaces as a crash rather than a clean shutdown. (2 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: BrokenResourceError (and ConnectionResetError) raised inside stdout_reader when the stdio_client context exits while the subprocess is still writing — the stream is already closed when send() is called, causing an unhandled exception that surfaces as a crash rather than a clean shutdown. (2 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: PR #2450 wraps each individual send() call inside the inner for-loop with try/except BrokenResourceError and returns early, which stops processing as soon as the stream is closed mid-loop — preventing both the exception propagation and any wasted work on subsequent lines. PR #2456 catches BrokenResourceError only at the outer except clause (same level as ClosedResourceError), which means the error can still escape from the inner send() calls before reaching that handler. #2456 also changes encoding_error_handler default from 'strict' to 'replace', which is a separate concern that should be evaluated independently. The granular inner-loop handling in #2450 is the more correct fix for the race described in issue #1960.

clusters.pick_reason: PR #2514 implements the positive side of spec-compliant cancellation (sending notifications/cancelled on timeout and caller cancellation), which subsumes #2493's change. #2493 only removes the incorrect error-response path in cancel(); a correct implementation must also emit the cancellation notification, which is what #2514 does. #2514 additionally covers the timeout scenario that #2493 does not address. The import of CancelledNotificationParams in #2514 confirms it is providing the complete replacement behavior, making #2493 redundant once #2514 lands.

clusters.pick_reason: PR #2514 implements the positive side of spec-compliant cancellation (sending notifications/cancelled on timeout and caller cancellation), which subsumes #2493's change. #2493 only removes the incorrect error-response path in cancel(); a correct implementation must also emit the cancellation notification, which is what #2514 does. #2514 additionally covers the timeout scenario that #2493 does not address. The import of CancelledNotificationParams in #2514 confirms it is providing the complete replacement behavior, making #2493 redundant once #2514 lands.

members.title: fix: don't send a response for cancelled requests
members.author: Zelys-DFKH
members.reason: [llm] duplicates #2514: The MCP cancellation protocol is not correctly implemented: the session sends an error response for cancelled requests (violating the spec's 'receivers MUST NOT send a response for a cancelled request') and does not send the required notifications/cancelled message on timeout or caller-initiated cancellation. Both PRs modify RequestResponder.cancel() and address the same spec section on cancellation semantics.
